## The project "Women at work" is online

  - Have fun
  - First contact with `R`
  - Use APIs like a pro
  - Use LLMs to help you solve it
  - Split tasks within the group

  - Only questions asked on the **forum** in Canvas will be answered
  - Deadline submission first part: **November 6th, 2026, 23:59**



## Exam

<br>

  - The *mock exam* is online 💣. The mock exam is longer (90mn) than the final exam this year (60mn)
  - The exam is similar in spirit and difficulty to the mock exam and to the quizzes.
  - Questions on the group project will be asked
  - If you attend the course and do the quizzes regularly, you’ll get familiar with the way I like asking questions...
  - Goal: you understand the concepts seen in the course and you can read and understand code.
  - ❗**You are not asked to write code**.



## What to expect in the exam

#### **True/False questions**, **multiple-choice questions**, and **multiple-correct options**.
  - Designed to test your understanding of the material.
  - Exactly same style  and structure as quizzes and mock exam
  - We do not invent wrong function parameters or misspell function names etc to mislead you!

#### Essay questions
  - Ask you to explain what you did in the group project and what we covered in the course.
  - Can be a piece of code to comment on, a question on the data or on the data pipeline, etc.


## What to expect in the exam

#### How to work your way efficiently through the exam

  - Work step-by-step through the code example. What happens in each parenthesis, on each line?
  - From the inner part to the outer part, from top to bottom.
  - If a code-example question refers to specific functions, you can always assume that the corresponding package is also loaded.
